questions.q: Name the two brothers of the narrator mentioned in the chapter and state one distinct detail about each that differentiates their economic status.
questions.a: The brothers are flejksy (elder) and fctokM+ (younger). flejksy is described as having a "gj ukyk" (thick/dense crop) and his house has "gj igkM+h unh dh jiV ij ikuh" (thick fog on the roof), suggesting relative prosperity. fctokM+ lives in a house where "fdrus lzksr gSa" (how many signs of poverty) and the roof has "mexdj iQy&iwQy vkSj vUu nsrh" (leaking, giving only drops). A wrong answer that treats both brothers as identical misses the text's deliberate contrast to show stratified impact of industrialization.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the mother (ekrk) refuses to leave her room when the narrator returns, and what this silence communicates about her agency.
questions.a: The mother's refusal ("ekrk rks cSB xbZ] vkjrh Hkh gks xbZ rkmQth") stems from grief over the lost landscape and betrayal by her sons who sold land. Her silence is not passivity but a withdrawal of consent — she rejects the transaction that turned "ekyok" into "lw[kk". A wrong answer framing her as merely "old and sad" ignores the political weight of her non-participation; she is the only character who never legitimizes the factory's presence.

questions.q: Apply the "foil" concept: Compare the nephew (nks) and the narrator as two educated figures. How does the nephew's desire to "ys tkus nksA mldk tks gS] j[ksA viuk tks gS mls ft,¡" (take what's his, leave the rest) contrast with the narrator's documentary impulse?
questions.a: The nephew embodies extractive modernity: he wants the monetary value ("ys tkus") but rejects the ecological/cultural baggage ("j[ks"). The narrator, though equally urban, returns to document ("ys[ku") and bear witness. The nephew severs roots; the narrator attempts (however inadequately) to archive them. A wrong answer that calls both "modern" flattens the critical distinction between complicity and testimony.

questions.q: Analyze how the sister-in-law (Hksu th) functions as a bridge between the domestic sphere and the industrial encroachment. Use her "poFk dk pk¡n" (husband's earnings) and her physical description ("fe^h dh m¡Qph dxkj ij isM+ksa osQ chp cSBs gq, ge pqipki mls iz.kke dj jgs Fks") as evidence.
questions.a: Hksu th sits on the "fe^h dh m¡Qph" (fruit of the tree/land) literally and metaphorically — her comfort ("poFk dk pk¡n") rests on the land's productivity, yet she is complicit in its sale ("ge pqipki mls iz.kke dj jgs Fks"). Her massive frame ("cM+h&cM+h ukosa") mirrors the bloated, unsustainable consumption the factory enables. She is the domestic face of ecological betrayal. A wrong answer focusing only on her weight misses the symbolic economy linking body, land, and capital.

questions.q: Evaluate the author's choice to give the villagers almost no direct speech except the mother's final rebuke ("uh ;kj isys ekrk fcBk;axk..."). Does this silence strengthen or weaken the critique of development?
questions.a: The silence strengthens the critique by making the villagers' erasure visceral — they are "ufn;ksa" (memories) before they are people. The mother's sole outburst becomes a thunderclap precisely because it breaks a 20-page hush. A wrong answer claiming "the author should have given them more voice" misunderstands the aesthetic strategy: the form enacts the content. The villagers' voicelessness *is* the violence of "mtkM+ dh vilH;rk".

questions.q: Create a 4-line dialogue between the elder brother (flejksy) and the mother (ekrk) set ten years after the factory opens, where flejksy defends the "development" and the mother counters with an image from the text.
questions.a:
flejksy: "देख माँ, पक्का मकान, स्कूटर, पोते की नौकरी — यही तो विकास है।"  
ekrk: "विकास? वो आम का बाग़ जहाँ तू झूला झूलता था, अब चिमनी का धुआँ उगलता है।"  
flejksy: "धुआँ ही तो रोटी देता है अब।"  
ekrk: "रोटी नहीं, बेटा, वो धुआँ तेरे बाप की चिता की राख है।"  
A poor answer writes generic arguments without anchoring in textual imagery (mango grove, chimney, father's pyre). The mother's line must echo the text's equation of factory smoke with ancestral cremation ("èkjrh osQ xHkZ osQ ikuh dks thoar j[k losaQA").
